questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसके हाइड्रॉक्साइड से भरे बर्तनों (पात्रों) पर दिए गए आरेख में दर्शाया गया चेतावनी चिह्न आवश्यक रूप से लगाया जाना चाहिए?
questions.text_english: The warning sign shown in the given figure must invariably be displayed/pasted on the containers which contain hydroxide of:
questions.image_description: A triangular red warning sign (corrosive hazard symbol) showing liquid dripping onto a hand causing damage, indicating a corrosive substance.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Sodium. Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is a strongly corrosive substance that can cause severe burns to skin and eyes on contact. The warning sign shown is the corrosive hazard symbol, which must be placed on containers of NaOH. Aluminium hydroxide, calcium hydroxide, and magnesium hydroxide are much milder and are not classified as dangerously corrosive substances requiring this warning sign.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) सोडियम है। सोडियम हाइड्रॉक्साइड (NaOH) एक अत्यंत संक्षारक पदार्थ है जो त्वचा और आंखों को गंभीर रूप से जला सकता है। दिया गया चेतावनी चिह्न संक्षारक पदार्थ का प्रतीक है, जो NaOH के पात्रों पर लगाया जाना आवश्यक है।
questions.topic: Properties of Sodium Hydroxide / Corrosive nature

questions.text: थर्मिट वेल्डिंग में ऐलुमिनियम चूर्ण का उपयोग किया जाता है क्योंकि:
questions.text_english: Aluminium powder is used in thermit welding because:

options.A: ऐलुमिनियम की आयरन के साथ अभिक्रिया अत्यधिक ऊष्माक्षेपी है।
options.B: ऐलुमिनियम को जब आयरन (III) ऑक्साइड के साथ गर्म किया जाता है, तो गलित आयरन प्राप्त होता है।
options.C: ऐलुमिनियम को जब आयरन (III) ऑक्साइड के साथ गर्म किया जाता है, तो गलित ऐलुमिनियम ऑक्साइड प्राप्त होता है जो रेल की पटरियों को जोड़ता है।
options.D: ऐलुमिनियम का गलनांक आयरन के गलनांक से कम है तथा गर्म करने पर ऐलुमिनियम और आयरन का गलित मिश्रातु बनता है जो रेल की पटरियों को जोड़ता है।

options_english.A: Its reaction with iron is highly exothermic.
options_english.B: When it is heated with iron (III) oxide, molten iron is obtained.
options_english.C: When it is heated with iron (III) oxide, molten aluminium oxide is obtained to join railway tracks.
options_english.D: Its melting point is low as compared to iron and a molten alloy of iron and aluminium is formed on heating which is used to join railway tracks.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). In thermit welding, aluminium powder reacts with iron (III) oxide (Fe₂O₃) upon heating. Aluminium, being more reactive than iron, displaces iron from its oxide. The reaction is: 2Al + Fe₂O₃ → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe. This produces molten iron at extremely high temperature, which is used to weld railway tracks. Option A is partially true but incomplete; the key reason is the production of molten iron, not merely heat release. Options C and D are factually incorrect.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। थर्मिट वेल्डिंग में ऐलुमिनियम चूर्ण, Fe₂O₃ के साथ गर्म करने पर अभिक्रिया करता है और गलित आयरन उत्पन्न होता है: 2Al + Fe₂O₃ → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe। इस गलित आयरन का उपयोग रेल की पटरियों को जोड़ने के लिए किया जाता है।
questions.topic: Reactivity Series / Displacement Reaction / Thermit Welding

questions.text: किसी परखनली में कुछ जिंक कणिकाएँ लेकर उसमें 2 mL सोडियम हाइड्रॉक्साइड विलयन मिलाया गया। जब इस मिश्रण को गर्म किया गया, तो बनने वाला उत्पाद है:
questions.text_english: A few pieces of granulated zinc are taken in a test tube and 2 mL of sodium hydroxide solution is added to it. When the contents are warmed, the product formed is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Na₂ZnO₂. Zinc is an amphoteric metal that reacts with sodium hydroxide solution upon heating. The reaction is: Zn + 2NaOH → Na₂ZnO₂ + H₂↑. The product formed is sodium zincate (Na₂ZnO₂) along with hydrogen gas. NaZnO₂ and Na₂ZnO do not represent the correct stoichiometric formula for sodium zincate, and NaZn(OH)₂ is not the product of this reaction.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) Na₂ZnO₂ है। जिंक एक उभयधर्मी धातु है जो NaOH के साथ गर्म करने पर अभिक्रिया करती है: Zn + 2NaOH → Na₂ZnO₂ + H₂↑। बना उत्पाद सोडियम जिंकेट (Na₂ZnO₂) है।
questions.topic: Amphoteric metals / Reaction of Zinc with NaOH

questions.text: दो भिन्न मिश्रातुओं को प्राप्त करने के लिए गलित कॉपर (प्राथमिक धातु) में निश्चित अनुपात में जिंक और टिन को पृथक-पृथक विलीन किया गया है। इनसे क्रमशः जो दो भिन्न मिश्रातु बनते हैं, उन्हें कहते हैं:
questions.text_english: Two metals zinc and tin are dissolved separately in definite proportions in molten copper (the primary metal) to obtain two different alloys respectively known as:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Brass and Bronze. Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc (Cu + Zn), while Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin (Cu + Sn). The question states that zinc is dissolved first in molten copper giving Brass, and tin is dissolved next giving Bronze — hence the order is Brass and Bronze. Solder is an alloy of lead and tin, so options B and D are incorrect. Option A reverses the correct order.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) पीतल और ब्रान्ज़ है। पीतल = कॉपर + जिंक, और ब्रान्ज़ = कॉपर + टिन। प्रश्न में पहले जिंक मिलाया गया (पीतल) फिर टिन (ब्रान्ज़), इसलिए उत्तर पीतल और ब्रान्ज़ है।

questions.text: वायु में प्राकृतिक गैस के दहन की ऊष्माक्षेपी अभिक्रिया दर्शाने वाला सही संतुलित रासायनिक समीकरण कौन-सा है?
questions.text_english: The correct balanced chemical equation showing exothermic reaction in which natural gas burns in air is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D): CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O + Energy. This equation is correctly balanced (1 C on each side, 4 H on each side, 4 O on each side) and correctly shows energy being released, indicating an exothermic reaction. Option A is unbalanced (only 1 O₂). Option B has 2CO₂ which is incorrect stoichiometry. Option C is balanced but does not mention Energy, so it does not indicate the exothermic nature.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O + ऊर्जा — यह समीकरण संतुलित है और ऊर्जा मुक्त होना दर्शाता है, जो ऊष्माक्षेपी अभिक्रिया का संकेत है।

questions.text: प्रोटीनों के संश्लेषण के लिए प्रयोग किया जाने वाला आवश्यक तत्त्व है:
questions.text_english: The essential element used in the synthesis of proteins is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Nitrogen. Proteins are made up of amino acids, and all amino acids contain nitrogen as part of their amino group (–NH₂). Nitrogen is therefore an essential element for protein synthesis. Phosphorus is essential for nucleic acids and ATP. Iron is needed for haemoglobin, and Magnesium is a component of chlorophyll — neither is directly part of protein structure.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) नाइट्रोजन है। प्रोटीन अमीनो अम्लों से बने होते हैं और सभी अमीनो अम्लों में नाइट्रोजन (–NH₂ समूह) होता है, इसलिए प्रोटीन संश्लेषण के लिए नाइट्रोजन आवश्यक है।

questions.text: किसी कोशिका विभाजन में गुणसूत्रों की संख्या आधी हो गई है। इस प्रकार के कोशिका विभाजन का प्रेक्षण कहाँ किया जाता है?
questions.text_english: The number of chromosomes in a cell division is halved. This kind of cell division is observed in:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Ovary and testis both. The type of cell division that halves the chromosome number is meiosis. Meiosis occurs in the gonads — both testes (to produce sperms) and ovaries (to produce eggs) — to form haploid gametes. It does not occur in all body cells (that is mitosis, which maintains the chromosome number). Hence options A, B, and D are incorrect.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) अंडाशय और वृषण दोनों में है। गुणसूत्रों की संख्या आधी करने वाला विभाजन अर्धसूत्री विभाजन (मियोसिस) है, जो वृषण और अंडाशय दोनों में होता है।

questions.text: एक कोशिकीय मोटी रुधिर वाहिकाओं को क्या कहते हैं?
questions.text_english: One-cell thick blood vessels are known as:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Capillaries. Capillaries are the smallest blood vessels and their walls are only one cell thick, which allows for efficient exchange of gases, nutrients, and waste products between blood and tissues. Arteries and veins have thicker, multi-layered walls. Alveoli are not blood vessels but air sacs in the lungs.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) केशिकाएँ है। केशिकाएँ सबसे छोटी रुधिर वाहिकाएँ हैं जिनकी दीवार केवल एक कोशिका मोटी होती है, जिससे रक्त और ऊतकों के बीच पदार्थों का आदान-प्रदान होता है।

questions.text: कायिक प्रवर्धन द्वारा उगाए गए पौधों के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही नहीं है?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following statements is not correct for the plants raised by vegetative propagation?

options.A: बीजों से उत्पन्न पौधों की तुलना में इन पर पुष्प और फल पहले उगते हैं।
options.B: उन पौधों को उगाया जा सकता है जो बीज उत्पन्न करने की क्षमता खो चुके हैं।
options.C: जनक पौधों की तुलना में, कायिक प्रवर्धन द्वारा उत्पन्न पौधों में अधिक विभिन्नताएँ होती हैं।
options.D: इस प्रकार उत्पन्न सभी पौधे आनुवंशिक रूप से जनक पौधे के समान होते हैं।

options_english.A: Can bear flowers and fruits earlier than those produced from seeds.
options_english.B: Those plants that have lost the capacity to produce seeds can be grown.
options_english.C: As compared to the parent plant, vegetatively propagated plants show more variations.
options_english.D: All the plants produced in this way are genetically similar to the parent plant.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). The statement in option C is NOT correct. Vegetative propagation is a form of asexual reproduction, so all plants produced are genetically identical to the parent plant — they show no more variations than the parent. In fact, vegetatively propagated plants show fewer or no variations compared to sexually reproduced (seed-grown) plants. Options A, B, and D are all correct statements about vegetative propagation.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। कायिक प्रवर्धन एक अलैंगिक प्रजनन है, इसलिए उत्पन्न पौधे जनक के समान होते हैं — उनमें अधिक विभिन्नताएँ नहीं होतीं। यह कथन गलत है।

questions.text: दिए गए आरेख A और B का प्रेक्षण कीजिए। जब किसी छुई-मुई (सुग्राही) पौधे को स्पर्श किया जाता है, तो उसकी पत्तियाँ मुड़ जाती हैं। इसका कारण है:
questions.text_english: Observe the given figures A and B. When chhui-mui (sensitive) plant is touched, its leaves fold. This is due to:

options.C: कोशिकाओं में जल की मात्रा में परिवर्तन

options_english.C: Change in amount of water in cells

questions.image_description: Figure A shows chhui-mui (Mimosa pudica) plant with leaves open. Figure B shows the same plant with leaves folded after being touched.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Change in amount of water in cells. When the sensitive plant (Mimosa pudica) is touched, a stimulus is transmitted and the cells at the base of the leaves rapidly lose water through osmosis, causing the cells to become flaccid. This loss of turgor pressure causes the leaves to droop and fold. This is not a hormonal response (which is slow) nor thermal or electromagnetic in nature.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) कोशिकाओं में जल की मात्रा में परिवर्तन है। स्पर्श होने पर पत्ती के आधार की कोशिकाएँ जल खो देती हैं, स्फीति दाब घटता है और पत्तियाँ मुड़ जाती हैं।

questions.text: 12 Ω के चार सर्वसम प्रतिरोधक आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार श्रेणीक्रम में संयोजित होकर वर्ग ABCD बनाते हैं। इस नेटवर्क के दो बिन्दुओं 1 और 2 के बीच प्रतिरोध है:
questions.text_english: Four identical resistors of 12 Ω each are connected in series to form a square ABCD as shown in the figure. The resistance of the network between the two points 1 and 2 is:
questions.image_description: A square circuit ABCD with four 12 Ω resistors (one on each side: AB, BC, CD, DA). Points 1 and 2 are at the top corners (A and B respectively). Current enters at point 1 (at A) and exits at point 2 (at B).
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 6 Ω. Points 1 and 2 are connected at A and B respectively. The direct path from 1 to 2 is through the resistor AB = 12 Ω. The other path is from A → D → C → B = 12+12+12 = 36 Ω. These two paths (12 Ω and 36 Ω) are in parallel. Combined resistance = (12 × 36)/(12 + 36) = 432/48 = 9 Ω. Wait — re-examining: points 1 and 2 are at A and B at the top. Path 1 (A to B directly) = 12 Ω. Path 2 (A → D → C → B) = 3 × 12 = 36 Ω. Parallel combination: R = (12 × 36)/(12 + 36) = 432/48 = 9 Ω. The correct answer should be (C) 9 Ω based on this calculation. However if points 1 and 2 are mid-points of sides AB and CD, the answer would differ. According to the diagram described, with points 1 at junction of A (between top-left) and 2 at top-right B, the parallel combination of 12 Ω and 36 Ω gives 9 Ω. The correct answer is (C) 9 Ω.

questions.text: यदि दो माध्यमों X और Y के निरपेक्ष अपवर्तनांक क्रमशः 6/5 और 4/3 हैं, तो X के सापेक्ष Y का अपवर्तनांक होगा:
questions.text_english: If the absolute refractive indices of two media X and Y are 6/5 and 4/3 respectively, then the refractive index of Y with respect to X will be:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 10/9. The refractive index of Y with respect to X is given by: ₓn_Y = n_Y / n_X = (4/3) / (6/5) = (4/3) × (5/6) = 20/18 = 10/9. Therefore, the refractive index of Y with respect to X is 10/9.

questions.text: मानव नेत्र में प्रवेश करने वाली प्रकाश किरणों का अधिकांश अपवर्तन नेत्र में निम्नलिखित में से किसके बाहरी पृष्ठ पर होता है?
questions.text_english: In the human eye, most of the refraction for the light rays entering the eye occurs at the surface of:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Cornea. In the human eye, the cornea (स्वच्छमंडल) is the transparent outermost layer and is responsible for most of the refraction of incoming light — approximately two-thirds of the eye's total focusing power. The crystalline lens fine-tunes the focus (accommodation), while the pupil only controls the amount of light and does not cause refraction. Aqueous humor also has a minor role.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) स्वच्छमंडल है। मानव नेत्र में आने वाले प्रकाश का अधिकांश (लगभग दो-तिहाई) अपवर्तन स्वच्छमंडल (कॉर्निया) की बाहरी सतह पर होता है।
questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.topic: Structure of Human Eye / Refraction in Eye

questions.text: किसी मिश्रातु के बने तार की प्रतिरोधकता सामान्यतः:
questions.text_english: The resistivity of a wire made of an alloy is generally:

options.A: उसके संघटक धातुओं की प्रतिरोधकता से निम्न होती है।
options.B: उसके संघटक धातुओं की प्रतिरोधकता से उच्च होती है।
options.C: उसके अनुप्रस्थ-काट के क्षेत्रफल में वृद्धि होने पर घट जाती है।
options.D: उसकी लंबाई में वृद्धि होने पर बढ़ जाती है।

options_english.A: Lower than that of its constituent metals.
options_english.B: Higher than that of its constituent metals.
options_english.C: Decreases with increase in its area of cross-section.
options_english.D: Increases with increase in its length.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). Alloys generally have higher resistivity than their constituent pure metals. This is because in an alloy, the irregular arrangement of different atoms disrupts the flow of electrons more than a pure metal lattice does. Resistivity is an intrinsic property of the material and does not depend on the dimensions (length or cross-section) of the wire, so options C and D are incorrect.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। मिश्रातु की प्रतिरोधकता उसके संघटक धातुओं से सामान्यतः अधिक होती है क्योंकि मिश्रातु में अनियमित परमाणु विन्यास इलेक्ट्रॉन प्रवाह को अधिक बाधित करता है।

questions.text: कोई बिम्ब किसी अवतल दर्पण के ध्रुव से 30 cm दूरी पर स्थित है। यदि इस बिम्ब का वास्तविक और उल्टा प्रतिबिम्ब इस दर्पण के सामने 60 cm दूरी पर बनता है, तो दर्पण की फोकस दूरी है:
questions.text_english: An object is placed at a distance of 30 cm from the pole of a concave mirror. If its real and inverted image is formed at 60 cm in front of the mirror, the focal length of the mirror is:
questions.solution: Using the mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u. For a concave mirror with new Cartesian sign convention: u = –30 cm, v = –60 cm (real image in front of mirror). So 1/f = 1/(–60) + 1/(–30) = –1/60 – 2/60 = –3/60 = –1/20. Therefore f = –20 cm. The negative sign confirms it is a concave mirror. The correct answer is (B) –20 cm.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से सभी अजैव-निम्नीकरणीय पदार्थों के समूह को पहचानिए।
questions.text_english: Identify from the following a group containing all non-biodegradable substances.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) DDT, Polyester, Glass. All three are non-biodegradable substances that cannot be broken down by microorganisms. DDT is a persistent pesticide, polyester is a synthetic polymer, and glass does not decompose. In option A, leather can slowly biodegrade. In option B, cotton and wood are biodegradable. In option D, silk and wool are natural fibres that are biodegradable.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) DDT, पॉलिएस्टर, काँच है। ये तीनों अजैव-निम्नीकरणीय पदार्थ हैं। अन्य विकल्पों में कपास, लकड़ी, रेशम, ऊन जैव-निम्नीकरणीय हैं।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): प्रोपेनैल और प्रोपेनोन संरचनात्मक समावयव हैं।
कारण (R): प्रोपेनैल और प्रोपेनोन दोनों के आण्विक सूत्र समान हैं।

Balance the following chemical equations:
(a) CO₂ + H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + O₂ + H₂O (Sunlight / Chlorophyll)

questions.solution: The balanced equations are: (a) 6CO₂ + 12H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ + 6H₂O (in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll). Verification: Left — 6C, 24H, 24O; Right — 6C, 24H, 24O. Balanced. (b) 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂ (on heating). Verification: Left — 2Pb, 4N, 12O; Right — 2Pb, 4N, 8O (in NO₂) + 2O (in PbO) + 2O (O₂) = 12O. Balanced.

Select from the following the members of same homologous series:

(2) Propanone (CH₃COCH₃)
(3) Propanoic acid (CH₃CH₂COOH)

key_points: Compounds (1) and (4) belong to the same homologous series — aldehydes (alkanals)

sub_questions.solution: Compounds (1) and (4) belong to the same homologous series — the aldehydes (alkanals). Compound (1) is propanal (CH₃CH₂CHO) with 3 carbons, and compound (4) is butanal (CH₃CH₂CH₂CHO) with 4 carbons. Both have the functional group –CHO and differ by one –CH₂– unit, which is the criterion for a homologous series. Compound (2) is a ketone and compound (3) is a carboxylic acid — different functional groups.

sub_questions.text_english: What happens to (i) the melting point, and (ii) the solubility of compounds as the molecular mass of the compounds in a homologous series increases?

key_points: (i) Melting point generally increases as molecular mass increases in a homologous series.
(ii) Solubility in water generally decreases as molecular mass increases.

sub_questions.solution: As the molecular mass of compounds in a homologous series increases: (i) The melting point (and boiling point) generally increases, because the larger molecules have stronger van der Waals forces between them, requiring more energy to overcome. (ii) The solubility in water generally decreases, because the longer carbon chain becomes more non-polar, reducing the ability of water (a polar solvent) to dissolve the compound.

sub_questions.text_english:
Write one function each of the following, in a seed:
(i) Seed coat (ii) Cotyledon (iii) Radicle (iv) Plumule

key_points: (i) Seed coat — protects the embryo from mechanical injury and desiccation.
(ii) Cotyledon — stores food (nutrients) for the developing embryo during germination.
(iii) Radicle — develops into the root system of the plant.
(iv) Plumule — develops into the shoot/stem of the plant.

sub_questions.solution: The functions of each part of a seed are: (i) Seed coat — It protects the internal parts of the seed (embryo) from external damage, dehydration, and entry of pathogens. (ii) Cotyledon — It stores food reserves (starch, proteins, fats) which nourish the embryo during germination until the seedling can photosynthesize. (iii) Radicle — It is the embryonic root that grows downward into the soil to absorb water and anchor the plant. (iv) Plumule — It is the embryonic shoot that grows upward and develops into the stem and leaves of the new plant.

sub_questions.text_english: Out of the two lenses, one concave and the other convex, state which one will diverge a parallel beam of light falling on it. Draw a ray diagram to show the principal focus of the lens.

key_points: A concave lens will diverge a parallel beam of light.
The diverged rays, when extended backward, appear to meet at the principal focus F on the same side as the incident light.

sub_questions.solution: A concave lens (diverging lens) will diverge a parallel beam of light falling on it. When parallel rays of light strike a concave lens, they spread out (diverge) after refraction. The diverged rays, when extended backwards on the same side as the incident light, appear to converge at a point called the principal focus (F) of the concave lens. The principal focus of a concave lens is virtual and lies on the same side as the incident light. [Ray diagram: Parallel rays → concave lens → diverged rays spreading outward; dotted lines extended backward meet at F on the left side of the lens]

questions.text_english: An electric fuse is rated 8 A. Can it be used with an electrical appliance of rating 5 kW, 200 V? Justify your answer.

key_points: Current drawn = P/V = 5000/200 = 25 A
The fuse rated 8 A cannot be used as 25 A > 8 A; the fuse would blow immediately.

questions.solution: No, the 8 A fuse cannot be used with the 5 kW, 200 V appliance. The current drawn by the appliance can be calculated using: I = P/V = 5000 W / 200 V = 25 A. sub_questions.solution: A decomposition reaction is a type of chemical reaction in which a single reactant breaks down into two or more simpler products. Three types with examples are: (1) Thermal decomposition (heat): CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. Calcium carbonate decomposes on heating to give calcium oxide and carbon dioxide. (2) Photolytic decomposition (light): 2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl₂ (in sunlight). Silver chloride decomposes in sunlight to give silver and chlorine gas. (3) Electrolytic decomposition (electricity): 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂ (by passing electricity). (ii) The decomposition of vegetable matter into compost is exothermic because the microorganisms that decompose the organic matter release energy in the form of heat during the process. The chemical bonds in complex organic molecules are broken down, releasing energy. This can be felt as warmth in a compost pile.

sub_questions.solution: Decomposition reactions are called the opposite of combination reactions because in a combination reaction, two or more reactants combine to form a single product, whereas in a decomposition reaction, a single reactant breaks down into two or more simpler products — the exact reverse process. Combination reaction: C + O₂ → CO₂. Reactants: Carbon (C) and Oxygen (O₂); Product: Carbon dioxide (CO₂). Here two substances combine into one. Decomposition reaction: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ (on heating). questions.solution: A reflex arc is the neural pathway involved in a reflex action, consisting of: receptor (detects stimulus) → sensory neuron → relay neuron (in spinal cord) → motor neuron → effector (muscle/gland). It is a rapid, automatic, involuntary response to a stimulus. In the human body, reflex arcs are formed in the spinal cord (though some, like pupillary reflex, involve the brain stem). Reflex arcs evolved in animals because they provide a survival advantage — they allow extremely rapid responses to potentially harmful stimuli (like withdrawing a hand from a hot surface) without the delay of sending signals all the way to the brain for processing. This swift response protects the body from damage and increases survival chances.

Attached and free earlobes are two variants found in human populations. The gene for free earlobe is dominant over attached earlobes.
(a) A man with attached earlobes marries a woman having free earlobes. 50% of their children have free earlobes and 50% have attached earlobes. Explain the inheritance of this trait and write the trait combinations of the progeny.
(b) Write the gene combinations of the father and the mother in the above case.

key_points: (a) Father (attached) genotype: aa; Mother (free, heterozygous) genotype: Aa. Cross: aa × Aa gives 50% Aa (free earlobe) and 50% aa (attached earlobe). Trait combinations of progeny: Aa (free earlobe) and aa (attached earlobe).
(b) Father's gene combination: aa; Mother's gene combination: Aa.

questions.solution: Let 'A' represent the dominant gene for free earlobe and 'a' represent the recessive gene for attached earlobe. (a) Since the man has attached earlobes, his genotype must be homozygous recessive: aa. The woman has free earlobes. Since 50% of their children have free earlobes and 50% have attached earlobes, the woman must be heterozygous: Aa. The cross is: aa (father) × Aa (mother) → offspring: 50% Aa (free earlobe) + 50% aa (attached earlobe). Trait combinations of progeny: Aa — free earlobe, aa — attached earlobe. This 1:1 ratio is characteristic of a monohybrid test cross. (b) Father's gene combination: aa (homozygous recessive — attached earlobe). Mother's gene combination: Aa (heterozygous — free earlobe).
questions.solution_hindi: A = स्वतंत्र कर्णपालि (प्रभावी), a = जुड़ी कर्णपालि (अप्रभावी)। पिता: aa, माता: Aa। संकरण: aa × Aa → 50% Aa (स्वतंत्र) + 50% aa (जुड़ी)। (ख) पिता: aa; माता: Aa।

questions.text_english: An object is placed at a distance of 20 cm from the optical centre of a concave lens and its image is formed on the same side of the lens as the object. If the distance of the image from optical centre of the lens is 10 cm, use lens formula to determine (i) focal length, and (ii) power of the lens in new Cartesian sign conventions.

key_points: u = –20 cm, v = –10 cm (image on same side as object, so negative)

questions.solution: Using new Cartesian sign conventions for a concave lens: Object distance u = –20 cm (object on left), Image distance v = –10 cm (image formed on the same side as the object, i.e., on the left). Using the lens formula: 1/f = 1/v – 1/u = 1/(–10) – 1/(–20) = –1/10 + 1/20 = –2/20 + 1/20 = –1/20. Therefore, focal length f = –20 cm. The negative sign confirms it is a concave (diverging) lens. (ii) Power of the lens: P = 1/f(in metres) = 1/(–0.20) = –5 D (dioptres). The negative power confirms it is a diverging lens.

questions.text_english: Resistance of a wire of length 1 m is 35 Ω at 20°C. If the diameter of the wire is 0·2 mm, determine the resistivity of the material of the wire at that temperature. How will the resistivity of the wire change if the length and diameter of the wire both are doubled? Justify your answer. (Given that π = 22/7)

key_points: Radius r = 0.1 mm = 0.1 × 10⁻³ m = 10⁻⁴ m
Resistivity does not change when length and diameter are doubled — it is an intrinsic property of the material.

questions.solution: Given: L = 1 m, R = 35 Ω, diameter = 0.2 mm, so radius r = 0.1 mm = 0.1 × 10⁻³ m = 10⁻⁴ m. Area of cross-section: A = πr² = (22/7) × (10⁻⁴)² = (22/7) × 10⁻⁸ m². Using the formula R = ρL/A, we get ρ = RA/L = 35 × (22/7) × 10⁻⁸ / 1 = 5 × 22 × 10⁻⁸ = 110 × 10⁻⁸ = 1.1 × 10⁻⁶ Ω·m. If both the length and diameter are doubled: the resistivity will NOT change. Resistivity (ρ) is an intrinsic property of the material of the conductor — it depends only on the nature and temperature of the material, not on its physical dimensions (length, area, diameter). Therefore, doubling length and diameter leaves resistivity unchanged.
questions.solution_hindi: r = 10⁻⁴ m, A = (22/7)×10⁻⁸ m²। ρ = RA/L = 35×(22/7)×10⁻⁸ = 1.1×10⁻⁶ Ω·m। लंबाई और व्यास दुगुना करने पर प्रतिरोधकता अपरिवर्तित रहेगी, क्योंकि यह पदार्थ का आंतरिक गुण है।

questions.text_english: Write the essential function performed by ozone at the higher levels of the atmosphere. How is it formed in the upper atmosphere? Write the name of the group of chemicals mainly responsible for the depletion of ozone layer.

key_points: Ozone absorbs harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun, protecting living organisms on Earth.
Formation: O₂ absorbs UV radiation and breaks into oxygen atoms (O); each O atom combines with another O₂ to form O₃ (ozone).
Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are the main group of chemicals responsible for ozone layer depletion.

questions.solution: Ozone (O₃) in the upper atmosphere (stratosphere) performs the essential function of absorbing harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation coming from the sun. Without this ozone layer, UV rays would reach Earth's surface and cause serious biological damage such as skin cancer, cataracts, and harm to ecosystems. Formation of ozone in the upper atmosphere: UV radiation from the sun causes oxygen molecules (O₂) to dissociate into free oxygen atoms (O + O). Each free oxygen atom then reacts with another oxygen molecule to form ozone: O + O₂ → O₃. The group of chemicals mainly responsible for ozone layer depletion is Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), which are synthetic compounds used in refrigerants and aerosol sprays.
questions.solution_hindi: ओज़ोन परत सूर्य की हानिकारक UV विकिरण को अवशोषित करती है। निर्माण: UV → O₂ → 2O; O + O₂ → O₃। ओज़ोन क्षय के लिए मुख्यतः क्लोरोफ्लुओरोकार्बन (CFCs) उत्तरदायी हैं।

sub_questions.solution: (i) Saturated hydrocarbons contain only single bonds between carbon atoms and are called alkanes. Example: Ethane — CH₃–CH₃. key_points: (i) Magnetic field lines are concentric circles around the wire; when current flows from X (top) to Y (bottom), by right-hand thumb rule, field lines go clockwise when viewed from above.
(ii) Right-Hand Thumb Rule (Maxwell's Corkscrew Rule): If the thumb of the right hand points in the direction of current, the curled fingers show the direction of magnetic field lines.

(iii) Fleming's Left Hand Rule: Stretch the thumb, index finger, and middle finger of the left hand mutually perpendicular; index finger → magnetic field direction, middle finger → current direction, thumb → force direction. For an electron moving in the given field, the current direction is opposite to electron motion; applying the rule gives the force direction as downward (into the page or as per the diagram).

sub_questions.solution: (i) When current flows from X (top) to Y (bottom) through the straight conductor, concentric circular magnetic field lines are formed around the wire. Applying the right-hand thumb rule with thumb pointing downward (X to Y), the field lines circle clockwise when viewed from above. (ii) Right-Hand Thumb Rule (also called Maxwell's Corkscrew Rule): If you hold the current-carrying conductor in the right hand with the thumb pointing in the direction of current flow, then the curled fingers of the right hand indicate the direction of the magnetic field lines around the conductor. (iii) Fleming's Left Hand Rule states: Stretch the thumb, index finger (fore finger), and middle finger of the left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular. If the index finger points in the direction of the magnetic field (B) and the middle finger points in the direction of current (I), then the thumb points in the direction of the force (F) on the conductor. Application: An electron moving to the right in a magnetic field directed to the right — since an electron is a negative charge, the conventional current direction is opposite to its motion (i.e., to the left). Applying Fleming's left hand rule with B pointing right and current pointing left, the force on the electron is directed downward (perpendicular to both B and current).

(ii) How would you make an electromagnet using a current carrying solenoid?

key_points: Solenoid: A coil of insulated copper wire wound in the form of a cylinder (helix), many turns close together.
Inside the solenoid, field lines are parallel and uniform (uniform magnetic field). Outside, field pattern resembles a bar magnet.
To make an electromagnet: insert a soft iron core inside the solenoid; when current flows, the core gets magnetised strongly. Removing current demagnetises it.

sub_questions.solution: A solenoid is a long coil of wire consisting of a large number of closely-wound circular turns of insulated copper wire, forming a cylindrical shape. (i) Magnetic field pattern: Inside the solenoid, the magnetic field lines are parallel to the axis of the solenoid and uniformly spaced, indicating a uniform and strong magnetic field. Outside the solenoid, the field lines curve around from one end to the other, resembling the magnetic field pattern of a bar magnet. The end where field lines emerge acts as the North pole and the end where they enter acts as the South pole. The region of uniform magnetic field is inside the solenoid along its central axis. The direction of current in the coil determines which end is north/south (right-hand rule for each turn). (ii) Making an electromagnet: Insert a soft iron rod (core) inside the solenoid. When electric current is passed through the solenoid, it generates a strong magnetic field that magnetises the soft iron core intensely, converting it into a powerful electromagnet. When the current is switched off, the soft iron loses its magnetism immediately, making it a temporary magnet — which is the advantage of an electromagnet over a permanent magnet.

sub_questions.text_english:
(i) 'The length of the small intestine in various animals depends on the food they eat.' Justify the statement.
(ii) Discuss the role of the pancreas and bile juice in the digestion of food in human beings.
(iii) How is the small intestine designed to absorb digested food?

key_points: (i) Herbivores have longer small intestine for cellulose digestion; carnivores have shorter intestine as meat is easier to digest.

(ii) Pancreas secretes pancreatic juice with enzymes (amylase, lipase, trypsin) to digest carbohydrates, fats, and proteins. Bile from liver emulsifies fats, increasing surface area for lipase action.
(iii) Small intestine has villi and microvilli (brush border) to increase surface area; villi have capillaries and lacteals for absorption of nutrients into blood and lymph.

sub_questions.solution: (i) The length of the small intestine varies depending on the diet: Herbivores (plant-eating animals) have a very long small intestine because plant material (cellulose) is difficult to digest and requires more time and surface area for digestion. Carnivores (meat-eating animals) have a shorter small intestine since proteins in meat are digested more rapidly and do not require as long a digestive tract. (ii) The pancreas secretes pancreatic juice into the small intestine containing enzymes: pancreatic amylase (digests starch into sugars), trypsin (digests proteins into amino acids), and lipase (digests fats into fatty acids and glycerol). Bile juice, produced by the liver and stored in the gall bladder, is released into the small intestine. It does not contain digestive enzymes but emulsifies fats — breaking large fat globules into smaller droplets — thereby increasing the surface area for lipase to act efficiently. (iii) The small intestine is specially designed for absorption: its inner wall has numerous finger-like projections called villi, which greatly increase the surface area for absorption. Each villus has a network of blood capillaries (to absorb glucose and amino acids into the blood) and lymph vessels called lacteals (to absorb fatty acids and glycerol). Microvilli on the surface of villi further multiply the absorptive surface area.

sub_questions.text_english:
(i) State the role of rings of cartilage present in the throat.
(ii) Discuss the role of the ribs and diaphragm when air is taken in during the breathing cycle.
(iii) Why do we get muscle cramps during heavy exercise? Explain.

key_points: (i) Cartilage rings in the trachea (throat) prevent it from collapsing, keeping the airway open for continuous air flow.

(ii) During inhalation, ribs move upward and outward (intercostal muscles contract), diaphragm contracts and moves downward — increasing thoracic volume, decreasing pressure, and drawing air into the lungs.
(iii) During heavy exercise, insufficient oxygen causes anaerobic respiration in muscles, producing lactic acid. Accumulation of lactic acid causes muscle cramps.

sub_questions.solution: (i) The rings of cartilage present in the trachea (throat/windpipe) serve the vital function of preventing the trachea from collapsing when air pressure inside changes during breathing. They keep the airway permanently open, ensuring a continuous, unobstructed flow of air to and from the lungs. (ii) During inhalation (breathing in): The intercostal muscles contract, causing the ribs to move upward and outward, increasing the volume of the chest (thoracic cavity). Simultaneously, the diaphragm — a muscular dome-shaped structure at the base of the chest — contracts and flattens, moving downward. Both these actions increase the volume of the thoracic cavity, which decreases the air pressure inside the lungs below atmospheric pressure, causing air to rush into the lungs. (iii) During heavy exercise, the muscles need more energy than can be supplied through normal aerobic respiration (using oxygen). As oxygen becomes insufficient, the muscles switch to anaerobic respiration: Glucose → Lactic acid + Energy. The lactic acid produced accumulates in the muscles and is not cleared fast enough. This buildup of lactic acid causes pain and cramps in the muscles. The cramps are relieved when sufficient oxygen is supplied and lactic acid is oxidised away.

key_points: Hydronium ion concentration increases 100 times (by a factor of 10² = 100) when pH decreases from 4 to 2.

sub_questions.solution: When the pH of a solution decreases from 4 to 2, the hydronium ion (H₃O⁺) concentration increases. sub_questions.solution: During indigestion, the stomach produces excess hydrochloric acid (HCl), making the stomach fluid highly acidic. The pH of the stomach fluid could be less than 2 (very acidic). To neutralise this excess acid and relieve pain and irritation, people use antacids as medicines. Common antacids include milk of magnesia, baking soda (sodium bicarbonate), and ENO. Milk of magnesia is a commonly used antacid. Its chemical name is Magnesium hydroxide, with the formula Mg(OH)₂. It is a mild base that neutralises the excess hydrochloric acid in the stomach: Mg(OH)₂ + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + 2H₂O.

sub_questions.text_english: How does the uterus prepare itself to receive and nurture the growing embryo? Explain.

key_points: The inner lining of the uterus (endometrium) thickens and becomes highly vascularised (rich in blood vessels) each month to receive the fertilized egg and provide nourishment to the developing embryo.

sub_questions.solution: Each month, the inner lining of the uterus (endometrium) thickens and becomes richly supplied with blood vessels in preparation for receiving a fertilized egg. This thickening provides a soft, nutrient-rich environment for the embryo to implant and grow. If a fertilized egg arrives, it embeds (implants) into this thickened lining, where it receives nutrients and oxygen from the mother's blood through the developing placenta.

key_points: If the egg is not fertilized, it lives for about 1 day.
The thickened uterine lining breaks down and is shed along with blood — this is called menstruation.

sub_questions.solution: When the egg released from the ovary is not fertilized by a sperm, it survives for approximately one day and then degenerates. Since fertilization has not occurred, there is no need for the thickened uterine lining (endometrium). Consequently, the thickened uterine lining breaks down, and its blood vessels rupture. The endometrial tissue, blood, and the unfertilized egg are shed out of the body through the vagina. This process is called menstruation (or the menstrual period/menstrual flow) and occurs roughly every 28 days.

sub_questions.solution: The developing embryo gets nutrition from the mother's blood through a special organ called the placenta. The placenta is a disc-shaped structure that develops and embeds in the wall of the uterus. It has a large surface area with villi that are in close contact with the mother's blood supply. Through the placenta, glucose, oxygen, water, vitamins, and other nutrients pass from the mother's blood into the embryo's blood. At the same time, carbon dioxide and other metabolic waste products produced by the embryo pass back into the mother's blood for elimination. The embryo and the mother's blood do not actually mix — exchange occurs across the thin membrane of the placenta. The embryo is connected to the placenta via the umbilical cord.

questions.text: किसी व्यक्ति ने सूर्य के श्वेत प्रकाश के महीन पुंज को किसी लघु द्वारक से किसी अँधेरे कमरे में प्रवेश कराया तथा प्रकाश पुंज के पथ में किसी काँच के प्रिज़्म को इस प्रकार रखा गया कि प्रकाश पुंज आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार प्रिज़्म के फलक AB पर आपतन करे। किसी पर्दे S को प्रिज़्म के दूसरी ओर, AC के सामने रखा गया। प्रिज़्म को धीरे-धीरे घुमाने पर, पर्दे पर वर्णों की आकर्षक पट्टी प्राप्त होती है। यह सूर्य के प्रकाश का स्पेक्ट्रम है।
questions.text_english: A person allowed a narrow beam of white light from the sun to enter a dark room through a small aperture and placed a glass prism in its path in such a manner that the beam falls on the face AB of the prism as shown in the figure. A screen S is placed on the other side of the prism, facing AC. On turning the prism slowly, a beautiful band of colours is obtained on the screen. It is the spectrum of sunlight.

questions.instruction_line_english: Read the case carefully and answer the questions that follow.

sub_questions.text: उस परिघटना का नाम लिखिए जिसके कारण कोई प्रिज़्म आपतित श्वेत प्रकाश को वर्णों की पट्टी में विभक्त कर देता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Name the phenomenon due to which a prism splits the incident white light into a band of colours.

key_points: The phenomenon is called Dispersion of light.

sub_questions.solution: The phenomenon due to which a prism splits incident white light into a band of colours is called Dispersion of light. Dispersion occurs because different colours (wavelengths) of light travel at different speeds in glass and are refracted by different amounts.

sub_questions.text: उपर्युक्त प्रकरण में सात वर्णों की पट्टी प्राप्त होने का कारण लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: State the reason of getting a band of seven colours in the above case.

key_points: White light is composed of seven different colours (VIBGYOR), each with a different wavelength. Glass has different refractive indices for different wavelengths, so each colour is refracted by a different angle, producing a band of seven colours.

sub_questions.solution: A band of seven colours (VIBGYOR: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red) is obtained because white light is actually a mixture of seven colours, each having a different wavelength. When white light passes through a glass prism, each colour travels at a slightly different speed in glass and is therefore refracted (bent) by a different amount. Violet light (shortest wavelength) is refracted the most and red light (longest wavelength) is refracted the least, resulting in the separation of white light into a spectrum of seven distinct colours.

sub_questions.text: नामांकित किरण आरेख की सहायता से, श्वेत प्रकाश के स्पेक्ट्रम का पुनर्योजन दर्शाने की प्रायोगिक व्यवस्था की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain with the help of a labelled ray diagram, an experimental arrangement to show the recombination of the spectrum of white light.

key_points: Two identical prisms placed inverted with respect to each other.
First prism disperses white light into VIBGYOR spectrum.
Second inverted prism recombines the seven colours back into white light.

sub_questions.solution: To show recombination of the spectrum of white light, two identical glass prisms are used. The first prism is placed in the path of a narrow beam of white light — it disperses the white light into its seven colours (VIBGYOR spectrum) on the other side. A second identical prism is placed inverted (upside down) with respect to the first prism, so that the dispersed colours from the first prism fall on the second prism. The second prism recombines all seven colours back together, and white light emerges from the other side. [Ray diagram: White light beam → First prism (VIBGYOR dispersed rays emerge) → Second inverted prism (seven colours recombine) → White light on screen.] This experiment demonstrates that white light is a mixture of seven colours and dispersion is a reversible process.

sub_questions.text: इन्द्रधनुष बनना दर्शाने के लिए नामांकित किरण आरेख खींचिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Draw a labelled ray diagram to show the formation of a rainbow.

key_points: Sunlight enters a water droplet, undergoes refraction (dispersion) at entry, total internal reflection at the back of the droplet, and refraction again at exit.
Violet light exits at a smaller angle (~40°) and red at a larger angle (~42°) to the original direction, producing the rainbow arc.

sub_questions.solution: Formation of a rainbow: A rainbow is formed in the sky after rainfall when sunlight interacts with tiny water droplets suspended in the atmosphere. The process involves three steps within each water droplet: (1) Refraction and dispersion: When sunlight enters a spherical water droplet, it slows down and disperses into its seven constituent colours (VIBGYOR) — violet refracts more than red. (2) Total internal reflection: The dispersed light undergoes total internal reflection at the back inner surface of the water droplet. (3) Refraction again: As the colours exit the droplet from the front, they undergo further refraction and spread out more. Red light exits at approximately 42° and violet at about 40° to the incident sunlight direction. An observer sees red at the top of the rainbow arc and violet at the bottom. [Ray diagram: Incident sunlight → spherical water droplet → dispersion at entry surface → total internal reflection at back → exit with colours separated, red at top, violet at bottom of the arc on a screen or to the observer's eye.]
